questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
For 22 years, the land records have shown a man as the owner of an 80-acre farm. The man has never physically occupied the land.
Nineteen years ago, a woman entered the farm. The character and duration of the woman's possession of the farm caused her to become the owner of the farm under the adverse possession law of the jurisdiction.
Three years ago, when the woman was not present, a neighbor took over possession of the farm. The neighbor repaired fences, put up "no trespassing" signs, and did some plowing. When the woman returned, she found the neighbor in possession of the farm. The neighbor vigorously rejected the woman's claimed right to possession and threatened force. The woman withdrew.
The woman then went to the man and told him of the history of activity on the farm. The woman orally told the man that she had been wrong to try to take his farm. She expressly waived any claim she had to the land. The man thanked her.
Last month, unsure of the effect of her conversation with the man, the woman executed a deed purporting to convey the farm to her son. The son promptly recorded the deed.
The period of time to acquire title by adverse possession in the jurisdiction is 10 years.
Who now owns the farm?

choices.A: The man, because the woman's later words and actions released title to the man.
choices.B: The neighbor, because the neighbor succeeded to the woman's adverse possession title by privity of possession.
choices.C: The son, because he succeeded to the woman's adverse possession title by privity of conveyance.
choices.D: The woman, because she must bring a quiet title action to establish her title to the farm before she can convey the farm to her son.

questions.explanation:
Contracts subject to statute of frauds
M arriage – promise in consideration of marriage
Y ear – contract cannot be completed within one year
L and – sale or other transfer of real property
E xecutor – promise to pay estate's debt from executor's personal funds
G oods – sale of goods for $500 or more
S uretyship – promise to pay another's debt

Mnemonic: MY LEGS

The statute of frauds requires that a conveyance of real property:

  • be in writing
  • identify the parties and property and
  • be signed by the donor (the person conveying the property).

Here, the woman acquired title to the man's farm by adverse possession. Although the woman later apologized to the man and orally waived her claim to the farm (Choice A), the man did not regain title because the woman's oral statement did not satisfy the statute of frauds since there was no signed writing. Therefore, the woman still owned the farm when she conveyed it to her son.

(Choice B) The neighbor did not succeed to the woman's adverse possession title because they lacked privity – a mutual or successive interest in the same property right. Instead, the neighbor took possession of the farm without the woman's permission and excluded her from the property.

But since the neighbor has only possessed the farm for 3 years, he has not acquired title by adverse possession and he has no other ownership interest.

(Choice D) The woman could have brought a quiet title action to establish her title to the farm (acquired by adverse possession) above all others before conveying it, but was not required to do so.

📌 Educational Objective

The statute of frauds requires that a conveyance of real property (1) be in writing, (2) identify the parties and property, and (3) be signed by the donor.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Wills & Other Donative Transfers § 6.3 (Am. Law Inst. 2003) (gifts of land subject to statute of frauds).
questions.zh-question:
三年前，当该女子不在场时，一位邻居接管并占有了该农场。邻居修理了栅栏，竖起了“禁止侵入”的标志，并进行了一些耕作。当该女子返回时，她发现邻居占有着该农场。邻居强烈拒绝了该女子声称的占有权，并以武力相威胁。该女子退让了。

随后，该女子找到该男子，告诉了他农场上活动的历史。该女子口头告诉该男子，她试图占有他的农场是错误的。她明确放弃了对该土地的任何权利主张。该男子感谢了她。

上个月，由于不确定她与该男子对话的效力，该女子签署了一份契约，意图将农场转让给她的儿子。儿子立即登记了该契约。

在该司法管辖区，通过侵权逆占获得所有权的时效期为10年。

现在谁拥有该农场？

zh-choices.A: 该男子，因为该女子后来的言语和行为将所有权归还给了该男子。
zh-choices.B: 邻居，因为邻居通过占有之关联继承了该女子的侵权逆占所有权。
zh-choices.C: 儿子，因为他通过转让之关联继承了该女子的侵权逆占所有权。
zh-choices.D: 该女子，因为她必须在将农场转让给儿子之前，提起确认产权诉讼以确立她对农场的所有权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Adverse Possession

核心考点 (Key Principle) 一旦时效占有（Adverse Possession）的法定时间届满，占有人即自动获得完整的所有权 (Legal Title)。此后，要将土地归还给原所有者，必须遵守反欺诈法 (Statute of Frauds)，即必须通过书面契约转让。
1 所有权何时转移？

题目指出该司法管辖区的时效期为 10 年。该女子在 19 年前进入农场，且其占有符合时效占有的所有要素。

这意味着，在 9 年前（19 - 10 = 9），该女子已经获得了农场的法律所有权 (Legal Title)。此时，原来的“土地记录所有者”（该男子）的所有权已被依法剥夺。

2 口头放弃有效吗？

这是本题最大的陷阱。该女子后来感到愧疚，口头告诉男子她放弃权利。但在法律上，她此时已经是“所有者”。

根据反欺诈法 (Statute of Frauds)，不动产权益的转让必须通过签署的书面文件 (Signed Writing) 进行。仅仅是口头道歉或口头放弃 (Oral Waiver) 是无效的。

✘ 选项 A 错误：因为没有书面契约，所有权并没有回流给该男子。
3 邻居是否获得了所有权？

邻居强行驱逐了该女子并占有了 3 年。虽然邻居的行为是敌对的，但时间太短（仅 3 年，未满 10 年）。

此外，邻居不能利用该女子的占有时间来凑够 10 年（即所谓的 Tacking / 叠加），因为 Tacking 需要占有人之间存在关联关系 (Privity)（如买卖、继承）。邻居是强行驱逐 (Ouster)，不存在 Privity。

✘ 选项 B 错误：邻居既没有 Privity，也没有占有足够的时间。
4 确认产权诉讼是必须的吗？

虽然该女子获得的头衔是“不可通过记录查询的” (Unmarketable title)，但这并不影响她拥有“法律所有权” (Legal Title)。

她可以提起确认产权诉讼 (Quiet Title Action) 来使产权变得可市场化 (Marketable)，但这并不是她转让财产的先决条件。她完全可以签署契约将她拥有的权益转让给儿子，只是儿子得到的也是一个有产权瑕疵风险的头衔，但这不影响所有权的转移本身。

✘ 选项 D 错误：诉讼不是转让所有权的必要条件。
5 结论

该女子是合法所有者。她的口头放弃无效。她签署契约将农场转让给儿子，该契约有效。因此，儿子 (The Son) 现在拥有农场。

正确答案：C

MBE Property Law Tip: Always check if the statutory period has already run. If yes, title has shifted!

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
The builder of a new house sold the house to a buyer, conveying it to the buyer by warranty deed. One year later, the buyer sold the house to a woman for $50,000 more than the buyer had paid, conveying it to the woman by a quitclaim deed.
Four months after moving in, the woman discovered a number of latent defects in the foundation that caused the house's basement to take on water during heavy rains. The woman contacted the builder about the problem. Toward the end of their heated conversation, the builder yelled at her, "So get it fixed!"
After the woman had the foundation repaired by a cement contractor at a cost of $25,000, she successfully sued the builder to recover that amount from him.
What is the most likely reason that the woman was successful?

choices.A: The court found an implied warranty of habitability from the builder to the buyer that was enforceable by a subsequent buyer.
choices.B: The court found that by paying the buyer $50,000 more for the house than the buyer had paid the builder, the woman did not get the benefit of her bargain.
choices.C: The court found that by yelling at the woman to "get it fixed," the builder had committed himself to paying for the repair.
choices.D: The court found that the defects in the foundation were a breach of the covenant of further assurances in the warranty deed from the builder to the buyer.

questions.explanation:
Implied warranty of habitability

(ie, implied warranty of fitness or suitability, quality, workmanlike construction)

Implied promise by builder, developer, or other commercial seller of new house that house was built in reasonably workmanlike manner & is suitable for living

Builder, developer, or other commercial seller liable for defects that interfere with buyer's ability to live in home

Buyer's damages based on cost of repairs to bring house into compliance with warranty

Under the implied warranty of habitability (ie, implied warranty of fitness or suitability), the builder of a new home impliedly guarantees that the home is habitable and fit for its intended purposes when sold. This allows buyers to recover damages for losses caused by the builder's defective construction or poor workmanship. And in most jurisdictions, this warranty extends to subsequent purchasers as to latent construction defects.

Here, the buyer purchased a new home from the builder and later sold it to the woman. After moving in, the woman discovered latent defects in the foundation that caused the house's basement to take on water during heavy rains (habitability concerns). Therefore, the most likely reason that the woman was successful against the builder is that the court found an implied warranty of habitability that was enforceable by her (a subsequent buyer).

(Choice B) Damages for breach of the implied warranty of habitability are based on the cost of repairs to bring the home into compliance with the warranty. Therefore, the additional $50,000 the woman paid to the buyer for the home does not affect her ability to recover $25,000 in repair costs from the builder for breach of this warranty.

(Choice C) The builder did not commit to paying for the repair by telling the woman to "get it fixed." Instead, he must pay for the repair because he is liable for latent construction defects under the implied warranty of habitability.

(Choice D) A warranty deed contains certain covenants of title, including the covenant of further assurances—ie, the grantor's promise to take any actions reasonably necessary to cure defects in title. But since defects in the foundation affect the physical condition (not title) of the property, this covenant does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

The implied warranty of habitability guarantees that a new home is habitable and fit for its intended purposes. This allows buyers to recover for losses caused by poor workmanship and, in most jurisdictions, allows subsequent purchasers to recover for losses caused by latent construction defects.

📚 References
  • 13 Am. Jur. 2d Building and Construction Contracts § 10 (2018) (duties implied by law).
questions.zh-question:
一栋新房的建造商将房屋出售给了一位买方，并通过担保契约将房屋转让给该买方。一年后，该买方以比其支付价高出50,000美元的价格将房屋出售给了一名女子，并通过免责契约将房屋转让给她。

搬入四个月后，该女子发现地基存在多处潜在缺陷，导致房屋地下室在暴雨期间进水。该女子就此问题联系了建造商。在他们激烈的交谈快结束时，建造商对她大喊：“那就去修好它！”

在该女子花费25,000美元请水泥承包商修复地基后，她成功起诉建造商，要求其赔偿该笔费用。

该女子胜诉最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 法院认定，建造商对买方存在一项可居住性默示担保，且该担保可由后续买方强制执行。
zh-choices.B: 法院认定，由于该女子为房屋支付的价比买方向建造商支付的价高出50,000美元，她没有获得其交易的预期利益。
zh-choices.C: 法院认定，建造商对该女子大喊“去修好它”，即表示他已承诺支付维修费用。
zh-choices.D: 法院认定，地基的缺陷违反了建造商向买方出具的担保契约中的进一步保证条款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：不动产法

Real Property: Implied Warranties

核心考点：可居住性默示担保 Implied Warranty of Habitability / Fitness

在普通法传统规则（买者自负 Caveat Emptor）下，房屋销售通常没有担保。但现代法律对新房建造商设立了例外：

  • 适用对象：新房的建造商或商业开发商。
  • 担保内容：房屋施工工艺精良，且适合居住。
  • 关键延伸：该担保通常延伸至后续买方 (Subsequent Purchasers)，只要在合理期限内发现潜在缺陷。
本题逻辑链条分析

1. 建造商身份：被告是新房建造商 (Builder of a new house)，属于该担保的责任主体。

2. 缺陷性质：地基缺陷导致进水，属于严重的潜在缺陷 (Latent Defects)，且影响居住 (Habitability)。

3. 原告身份：原告是二手买家 (Subsequent Buyer)。虽然她与建造商之间没有直接合同关系 (Privity of Contract)，但现代法院倾向于保护后续买家，因为建造商处于控制建筑质量的最佳位置。

4. 契约类型无关性：虽然原告是通过“免责契约” (Quitclaim Deed) 买房，但这只免除了中间卖家的产权担保责任，并不切断建造商对房屋物理质量的法定担保责任。

选项深度解析
选项 A (正确答案)
法院认定存在可居住性默示担保，且该担保可由后续买方强制执行。

理由：这是现代不动产法的多数规则。对于潜在的建筑缺陷，建造商的责任不因房屋转手而消失。
选项 B (错误)
关于“交易预期利益” (Benefit of Bargain)。

理由：买贵了或者买便宜了，与建造商是否违约无关。损害赔偿是基于修复成本，而非买卖差价。
选项 C (错误)
关于“口头承诺”。

理由：建造商气急败坏喊出的 "Get it fixed" 缺乏合同成立的意图 (Intent)，不足以构成新的有约束力的口头合同。
选项 D (错误 - 常见陷阱)
关于“进一步保证条款” (Covenant of Further Assurances)。

理由：这是产权担保 (Title Covenant) 的一部分，用于解决产权瑕疵（如签字遗漏、文件错误），不适用于房屋的物理状况或建筑质量。
💡 MBE 抢分技巧

区分“产权”与“质量”：

看到题目中出现 Warranty Deed 或 Quitclaim Deed 时，首先判断题目考的是产权归属/瑕疵 (Title Issues) 还是房屋物理缺陷 (Physical Defects)。

  • 如果是物理缺陷（如本题的地基、漏水），通常适用 Implied Warranty of Habitability，Deed 的类型通常是干扰项。
  • 如果是产权纠纷（如抵押权未清除），才需要分析 Deed 中的 Covenants。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A seller who owned land entered into a valid written agreement to sell the land to a buyer by installment purchase. The contract stipulated that the seller would deliver to the buyer, upon payment of the last installment due, "a warranty deed sufficient to convey a fee simple title." The contract contained no other provision that could be construed as referring to title.
The buyer entered into possession of the land. After making 10 of the 300 installment payments obligated under the contract, the buyer discovered that there was outstanding a valid and enforceable mortgage on the land, securing the payment of a debt in the amount of 25 percent of the purchase price that the buyer had agreed to pay. There was no evidence that the seller had ever been late in payments due under the mortgage, and there was no evidence of any danger of insolvency of the seller. The value of the land was then four times the amount due on the debt secured by the mortgage.
The buyer quit possession of the land, stopped making payments on the contract, and demanded that the seller repay the amounts that the buyer had paid under the contract. After the seller refused the demand, the buyer sued the seller to recover damages for the seller's alleged breach of the contract.
Should damages be awarded to the buyer?

choices.A: No, because an installment purchase contract is treated as a security device.
choices.B: No, because the time for the seller to deliver marketable title has not arrived.
choices.C: Yes, because an installment purchase contract is treated as a mortgage, and the outstanding mortgage impairs the buyer's equity of redemption.
choices.D: Yes, because in the absence of a contrary express agreement, an obligation to convey marketable title is implied.

questions.explanation:
"Red flags" for marketable title

  • Covenants
  • Easements
  • Leases
  • Liens
  • Gaps in chain of title
  • Boundary disputes
  • Existing zoning violations
  • Adverse possession

All land-sale contracts have an implied warranty that the seller will convey marketable title to the buyer upon closing unless otherwise stated. Title does not have to be perfect to be marketable. However, it must be reasonably free from doubt and under no threat of litigation, such that a reasonable person would accept and pay for it. In the case of an installment land contract—ie, one in which the buyer takes possession of the property and pays the purchase price over time—the seller need not deliver marketable title until the price is fully paid.

Here, after making 10 of the 300 installment payments, the buyer discovered that there was an outstanding mortgage on the land. Although an existing mortgage can render title unmarketable, the seller does not need to deliver marketable title until the buyer has made all installment payments. Therefore, damages should not be awarded to the buyer because the time for the seller to deliver marketable title has not arrived (Choice D).

(Choice A) The fact that an installment land contract is treated as a security device (namely, a mortgage) does not prevent the buyer from recovering damages if the seller is unable to deliver marketable title when it is due (not seen here).

(Choice C) An installment land contract is often treated as a mortgage, so the seller can bring a foreclosure action to regain possession of the property if the buyer defaults on payments. Although the buyer stopped making payments here, the seller has not yet attempted to enforce the contract. As a result, the buyer's equity of redemption (ie, pre-foreclosure right to cure the default by paying the entire past-due amount) is not at issue.

📌 Educational Objective

Under an installment land contract, the seller does not need to deliver marketable title until the purchase price is fully paid.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Mortgages § 3.4 (Am. Law Inst. 1997) (installment land contracts).
  • 77 Am. Jur. 2d Vendor and Purchaser § 93 (2020) (marketable title).
questions.zh-question:
一位拥有土地的卖方与一位买方签订了一份有效的书面协议，以分期付款购买的方式向其出售该土地。合同规定，卖方应在买方付清最后一期应付款项后，向买方交付“一份足以转让完全所有权（fee simple title）的产权保证书（warranty deed）”。合同中没有其他可被解释为与所有权相关的条款。

买方占有了该土地。在支付了合同规定的300期分期付款中的10期后，买方发现该土地上存在一笔有效且可强制执行的抵押，该抵押担保了一笔债务的偿还，债务金额为买方同意支付的购买价格的25%。没有证据表明卖方曾延迟支付抵押贷款的到期款项，也没有证据表明卖方有任何破产的风险。当时该土地的价值是抵押所担保债务到期金额的四倍。

买方放弃了对土地的占有，停止支付合同款项，并要求卖方退还买方根据合同已支付的款项。在卖方拒绝该要求后，买方起诉卖方，以卖方涉嫌违约为由要求损害赔偿。

买方应否获得损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为分期付款购买合同被视为一种担保工具。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为卖方交付可售所有权（marketable title）的时间尚未到来。
zh-choices.C: 是的，因为分期付款购买合同被视为一种抵押，而未偿还的抵押损害了买方的赎回权（equity of redemption）。
zh-choices.D: 是的，因为在没有相反明确约定的情况下，转让可售所有权（marketable title）的义务是默示的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Estate Contracts / Marketable Title

核心法律原则：交付时间 在分期付款土地合同 (Installment Land Contract) 中，卖方交付可售所有权 (Marketable Title) 的义务，通常只有在买方支付完最后一笔款项时才产生，而不是在合同签订时。

合同签订 (Day 1)

买方开始占有土地，卖方保留法定所有权 (Legal Title)。

第 10 期付款 (现状)

买方发现抵押贷款。关键点：此时卖方尚无义务交付无瑕疵产权。

第 300 期付款 (未来)

交付日 (Law Day)：这是卖方必须清除抵押并交付产权保证书的时刻。

案情深度分析

本题考察的是“预期违约”与“履行时间”的界限。

1. 现状并非违约： 只要卖方在最后交割日（第300期付款时）能提供可售所有权，中间存在的抵押并不构成违约。卖方完全有权利用买方的分期付款来偿还自己的抵押贷款。

2. 无破产风险： 题目特意指出卖方没有破产风险 (insolvency) 且土地价值远高于债务。这意味着卖方有能力在未来清除产权瑕疵。

3. 买方反应过度： 买方在第10期就要求退款并起诉，属于过早行动。因为卖方交付产权的时间（Time for performance）尚未到来。

✅ 正确答案：B
不应赔偿，因为卖方交付可售所有权的时间尚未到来。

关于选项 D 的误区：
虽然合同确实默示了“可售所有权”的义务（选项D的前半部分正确），但该选项忽略了时间要素。默示义务是存在的，但它只有在合同约定的交付时间（即付清全款时）才需要被履行。

💡 MBE 考试技巧
遇到 Installment Land Contract 的题目时，请记住：
  • 这不同于普通的房屋买卖（Closing通常在30-60天）。
  • 分期合同可能持续数十年。
  • 只要卖方不是“无可救药地破产”或存在欺诈，买方通常不能因为中间存在的留置权（Lien）或抵押（Mortgage）而解除合同，因为卖方有权在最后一刻“修补”产权。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A buyer validly contracted in writing to buy improved land from a seller. The contract had no contingencies and was silent as to risk of loss if there was damage to, or destruction of, property improvements between contract and closing, and as to any duty to carry insurance. As soon as the parties signed the contract, the seller (who had already moved out) canceled her insurance covering the land. The buyer did not know this and did not obtain insurance. A few days later, three weeks before the agreed closing date, the building on the land was struck by lightning and burned to the ground.
There is no applicable statute.
In an appropriate action, the buyer asserted the right to cancel the contract and to recover his earnest money. The seller said that because the risk of fire loss had passed to the buyer before the fire, the buyer must perform.
If the seller prevails, what will be the most likely explanation?

choices.A: Once the parties signed the contract, only the buyer had an insurable interest and so could have protected against this loss.
choices.B: The buyer's constructive possession arising from the contract gave him the affirmative duty of protecting against loss by fire.
choices.C: The seller's cancellation of her casualty insurance caused the risk of loss to transfer to the buyer.
choices.D: Upon execution of the contract, the buyer became the equitable owner of the land under the doctrine of equitable conversion.

questions.explanation:
Equitable conversion under land-sale contract

▶
Contract
formation
Executory period
Closing
Legal title
Equitable title
Seller
Buyer
Seller has full ownership
Buyer has full ownership

A majority of jurisdictions apply the doctrine of equitable conversion when a land-sale contract is silent regarding the risk of loss (as seen here). Under this doctrine, the risk of loss is placed on the party with equitable title at the time the property was destroyed. The buyer receives equitable title once the contract is formed and can be specifically enforced. If no conditions/contingencies appear in the contract (eg, a condition that the buyer secure financing before closing), the contract is specifically enforceable as soon as it is formed. Therefore, the seller likely prevailed because the buyer was the equitable owner of the land when the building was destroyed.

(Choices A, B & C) Unless otherwise provided, a land-sale contract does not impose a duty on either the seller or the buyer to carry property insurance. Therefore, neither the signing of the contract nor the seller's cancellation of the insurance transferred the risk of loss to the buyer.

📌 Educational Objective

Unless otherwise provided, the doctrine of equitable conversion places the risk of loss on the buyer once the land-sale contract is formed and can be specifically enforced.
questions.zh-question:
买方与卖方签订了一份有效的书面合同，购买一块已改良的土地。该合同没有附带任何意外事件条款，并且对于合同签订日至交割日期间，若财产改良物受损或被毁的损失风险，以及购买保险的义务，均未作规定。合同一经双方签署，卖方（其已搬离）便取消了该土地的保险。买方对此并不知情，也未购买保险。几天后，在约定的交割日期前三周，该土地上的建筑物被闪电击中，并被夷为平地。

本案没有适用的成文法。

在适当的诉讼中，买方主张有权解除合同并要求返还其定金。卖方称，由于火灾损失的风险在火灾发生前已转移给买方，因此买方必须履行合同。

如果卖方胜诉，最可能的解释是什么？

zh-choices.A: 一旦双方签订合同，只有买方拥有可保利益，因此本可以投保以防范此项损失。
zh-choices.B: 由合同产生的买方的推定占有，使其负有防止火灾损失的积极义务。
zh-choices.C: 卖方取消其灾害保险的行为，导致损失风险转移给了买方。
zh-choices.D: 合同一经签署，根据衡平法转换原则 (doctrine of equitable conversion)，买方即成为该土地的衡平法上的所有权人。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Risk of Loss
核心考点：衡平法转换原则 (Doctrine of Equitable Conversion)

这是普通法（Common Law）中的一项重要原则。其核心思想是：一旦双方签订了可强制执行（Specifically Enforceable）的土地买卖合同，衡平法将视“应做之事为已做之事”（Equity regards as done that which ought to be done）。

合同签署 (Contract Signed)
此时发生所有权分离：
1. 买方获得衡平法所有权 (Equitable Title)
2. 卖方保留法定所有权 (Legal Title) 作为收款担保
风险转移 (Risk of Loss)
根据普通法，损失风险随衡平法所有权转移。因此，买方承担房屋损毁的风险。
交割 (Closing)
法定所有权最终转移给买方。

为什么选项 D 是正确的？

正确答案 D

解析：题目明确指出“没有适用的成文法”（There is no applicable statute）。这意味着我们必须适用普通法规则。

根据衡平法转换原则，只要合同没有意外事件条款（Contingencies）且可强制执行，买方在签字那一刻就成为了土地的衡平法所有权人 (Equitable Owner)。

因此，即使卖方还持有法定地契（Legal Title），房屋被闪电击毁的风险（Risk of Loss）已经转移给了买方。买方必须履行合同支付全款，尽管房子已经没了。

其他选项为什么错误？

选项 A 错误

可保利益 (Insurable Interest)： 双方都有可保利益。卖方有法定所有权，买方有衡平法所有权。并不是“只有”买方可以投保。

选项 B 错误

占有 (Possession)： 风险转移的依据是所有权 (Title) 的性质，而不是占有。即使买方还没有搬进去（没有占有），根据普通法，风险依然转移了。

选项 C 错误

保险义务： 除非合同另有规定，普通法下卖方没有义务为买方的利益维持保险。卖方取消保险的行为虽然冷酷，但在法律上并没有改变风险承担的规则。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧：

注意题目中的关键词 "There is no applicable statute"。

在现实生活中，许多州采用了《统一卖方与买方风险法》(Uniform Vendor and Purchaser Risk Act, UVPRA)，该法规定风险在交付占有或转移法定所有权时才转移。

但 MBE 题目如果排除了成文法，就是在考你古老的普通法规则 (Common Law Rule)：签字即转移风险。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man owned a residential lot improved with a dwelling and conveyed it for a valuable consideration to a buyer. The dwelling had been constructed by a prior owner. The buyer had inspected the dwelling prior to the purchase and discovered no defects. After moving in, the buyer became aware that sewage seeped into the basement when the toilets were flushed. The man said that this defect had been present for years and that he had taken no steps to hide this fact from the buyer. The buyer paid for the necessary repairs and brought an appropriate action against the man to recover his cost of repair.
If the buyer wins, what will be the likely reason?

choices.A: The buyer made a proper inspection.
choices.B: The man breached the implied warranty of habitability and fitness for purpose.
choices.C: The man failed to disclose a latent defect.
choices.D: The situation constitutes a health hazard.

questions.explanation:
Seller's duty to disclose
Common law (minority) rule Caveat emptor No duty to disclose property defects unless otherwise provided
Modern (majority) rule Commercial property
Residential property Must disclose known material defects that buyer could not reasonably discover • Exception: “as is” clause or specific disclaimers without seller's fraud

The majority of jurisdictions impose a duty on sellers of residential property to disclose any material defects that are known to the seller and cannot be reasonably discovered by the buyer. A defect is material if it:

  • substantially affects the value of the residence
  • impacts the health or safety of a resident or
  • affects the desirability of the residence to the buyer.

Here, the man admitted that he had known for years that sewage seeped into the basement when the toilets were flushed. This clearly material defect could not be, and was not, reasonably discovered by the buyer after inspecting the dwelling. Therefore, the buyer will likely win because the man breached his duty to disclose this latent defect.

(Choice A) A proper or reasonable inspection may not unearth every defect with a property. As a result, the duty to disclose defects that are not readily discoverable applies even when a buyer conducts an inspection.

(Choice B) The warranty of habitability and fitness* is implied in almost all jurisdictions in a contract for the sale of a newly constructed residence, so it does not apply here.

*This is also referred to as the implied warranty of suitability, quality, or workmanlike construction.

(Choice D) The mere fact that the defect in question poses a health hazard is not enough to impose liability on the seller. For example, the man would not be liable for the hazardous defect if he had been unaware of the defect or if he had included an “as is” clause to disclaim the duty to disclose.

📌 Educational Objective

A seller of residential property has a duty to disclose any known material defects that cannot be reasonably discovered by the buyer.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子拥有一块建有住宅的住宅用地，并以有价对价将其转让给了一位买方。该住宅由前一任所有者建造。买方在购买前检查了该住宅，并未发现任何瑕疵。搬入后，买方发现冲马桶时，污水会渗入地下室。该男子称，此瑕疵已存在多年，且他未采取任何措施向买方隐瞒这一事实。买方支付了必要的维修费用，并对该男子提起了适当的诉讼，以追回其维修成本。

如果买方胜诉，最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 买方进行了适当的检查。
zh-choices.B: 该男子违反了默示的可居住性与适用性保证。
zh-choices.C: 该男子未能披露一个潜在瑕疵。
zh-choices.D: 该情况构成了健康危害。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property / Contracts
正确答案：C 该男子未能披露一个潜在瑕疵。
(The man failed to disclose a latent defect.)
核心考点：卖方的披露义务

本题考察的是住宅房地产销售中，卖方对房屋瑕疵的披露责任。在现代法律规则下，这一领域发生了从“买者自慎”到“强制披露”的转变。

传统普通法
(Common Law)		 现代多数派规则
(Modern Majority Rule)
Caveat Emptor
(买者自慎)		 披露义务
(Duty to Disclose)
卖方无义务披露瑕疵，除非存在积极隐瞒或欺诈。 卖方必须披露已知的、重大的、且买方无法合理发现的潜在瑕疵。
本案逻辑推理

要让买方胜诉，必须满足现代规则下的三个要素：

  1. 已知 (Known): 题目明确指出卖方知道该问题已存在多年。
  2. 重大 (Material): 污水渗入地下室属于严重的卫生和结构问题，显然是重大瑕疵。
  3. 潜在/不易发现 (Latent/Not reasonably discoverable): 题目指出买方进行了检查但未发现（因为只有冲水时才发生，且可能需要特定条件），这属于潜在瑕疵 (Latent Defect)。

结论： 尽管卖方没有积极隐瞒（Active Concealment），但在现代规则下，他对已知的潜在重大瑕疵保持沉默（Silence）本身就构成了违约或欺诈性不披露。

为什么其他选项是错误的？

❌ 选项 A：买方进行了适当检查
虽然买方进行了检查，但这只是证明瑕疵是“潜在的”一个前提条件。买方胜诉的法律依据是卖方“未披露”，而不是买方“已检查”。

❌ 选项 B：默示的可居住性保证 (Implied Warranty of Habitability)
这是本题最大的陷阱。
该保证通常只适用于新房销售（由建筑商/开发商出售给第一任买家）。本题中，房屋是由“前任所有者”建造的，且卖方只是普通房主（二手房交易），因此不适用此默示保证。

❌ 选项 D：构成健康危害
“健康危害”说明了瑕疵的重大性 (Materiality)，但仅有危害本身并不足以让卖方承担责任。如果卖方自己也不知道这个危害，或者买方很容易就能发现这个危害，卖方可能就不承担责任。责任的来源是“知情不报”。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A grantor executed an instrument in the proper form of a warranty deed purporting to convey a tract of land to his church. The granting clause of the instrument ran to the church "and its successors forever, so long as the premises are used for church purposes." The church took possession of the land and used it as its site of worship for many years. Subsequently, the church decided to relocate and entered into a valid written contract to sell the land to a buyer for a substantial price. The buyer wanted to use the land as a site for business activities and objected to the church's title. The contract contained no provision relating to the quality of title the church was bound to convey.
There is no applicable statute.
When the buyer refused to close, the church sued the buyer for specific performance and properly joined the grantor as a party.
Is the church likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the grantor's interest prevents the church's title from being marketable.
choices.B: No, because the quoted provision is a valid restrictive covenant.
choices.C: Yes, because a charitable trust to support religion will attach to the proceeds of the sale.
choices.D: Yes, because the grantor cannot derogate from his warranty to the church.

questions.explanation:
Fee simple estates
Type Language Future interest
Indefeasible
Fee simple absolute
  • “To A”
  • “To A and his heirs”
 None
Defeasible (Durational)
Fee simple determinable
  • “so long as”
  • “during”
  • “until”
 Grantor’s possibility of reverter
Third party’s executory interest
(ie, fee simple subject to executory limitation)
Defeasible (Conditional)
Fee simple subject to condition subsequent
  • “but if”
  • “provided that”
  • “unless”
 Grantor’s right of entry

In a land-sale contract, the seller promises to deliver marketable title to the buyer upon closing. Title is marketable if it is reasonably free from doubt and under no threat of litigation such that a reasonable person would accept and pay for it. If the seller fails to satisfy this promise, the buyer can rescind the contract and refuse to close.

Here, the church has a defeasible fee because its title will automatically terminate if the specified event or condition occurs — ie, when the land is no longer used for church purposes. If the buyer were to purchase the land and use it for business purposes, the specified event would occur. The buyer’s title would then terminate and revert back to the grantor. As a result, the church cannot deliver marketable title and its suit against the buyer will likely fail.

(Choice B) A restrictive covenant is a promise to do or not do something on one’s land that has no impact on title. Since the quoted provision will divest the church (or its assigns) of title if the land is no longer used for church purposes, it is not a restrictive covenant but a defeasible fee.

(Choice C) Attaching the sale proceeds to a charitable trust will have no impact on the church’s ability to convey marketable title. This merely means that a trustee will hold those proceeds at the church’s request for some charitable purpose and title will still terminate if the specified condition occurs.

(Choice D) The grantor cannot and has not derogated any warranty (ie, covenant of title) to the church. He had the right to convey the church a defeasible fee and the right to retain a possibility of reverter in that land.

📌 Educational Objective

Marketable title is title that is reasonably free from doubt and under no threat of litigation such that a reasonable person would accept and pay for it. The owner of a defeasible fee cannot convey marketable title since title will automatically terminate upon the happening of a specified event or condition.

📚 References
  • 77 Am. Jur. 2d Vendor and Purchaser § 93 (2020) (marketable title).
questions.zh-question:
一位出让人以担保契据的适当形式签署了一份文书，意图将其一片土地转让给其教会。该文书的授予条款规定，土地授予教会“及其永久继承人，只要该处所被用于教会目的”。教会占有了该土地，并多年将其用作礼拜场所。后来，教会决定搬迁，并签订了一份有效的书面合同，以可观的价格将该土地出售给一位买方。买方希望将该土地用作商业活动场所，并对教会的产权提出了异议。合同中没有包含关于教会必须转让的产权质量的条款。

没有适用的成文法。

当买方拒绝完成交易时，教会起诉买方要求强制履行，并适当地将出让人列为当事人。

教会可能胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为出让人的权益使得教会的产权不具可售性。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为所引用的条款是一个有效的限制性契约。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为支持宗教的慈善信托将附加于销售收益上。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为出让人不能减损其对教会的担保。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Marketable Title
核心考点：可售产权 (Marketable Title)

在每一份土地销售合同中（除非另有说明），卖方都默示承诺提供可售产权。这意味着产权必须合理地没有疑问，且没有诉讼风险。

案件逻辑分析

1. 确定产权类型：
出让人使用的语言是“so long as”（只要），这是典型的期限性语言 (Durational Language)。这创造了可决定的完全所有权 (Fee Simple Determinable)。

这意味着：如果土地不再用于教会目的，产权将自动终止并复归给原出让人。原出让人保留了复归可能性 (Possibility of Reverter)。

2. 评估产权质量：
教会拥有的不是绝对的完全所有权 (Fee Simple Absolute)，而是随时可能因为违反条件而丧失的产权。

3. 结合买方意图：
买方明确表示要将土地用于“商业活动”。一旦交易完成并改变用途，出让人的“复归可能性”就会被触发，买方将立即失去土地。这使得该产权面临极大的诉讼风险和实质性缺陷。

✅ 正确答案：选项 A

"No, because the grantor's interest prevents the church's title from being marketable."

解析：
由于出让人保留了复归可能性（Grantor's interest），教会无法向买方提供一个完整的、没有被没收风险的产权。一个理性的买家不会接受这种只要一使用（商业用途）就会自动丧失的土地。因此，教会违反了默示的可售产权 (Marketable Title) 承诺，无法强制买方履行合同。

为什么其他选项是错的？
❌ 选项 B (Restrictive Covenant)
限制性契约通常只导致损害赔偿或禁令，而不会导致产权丧失（Forfeiture）。本题中的措辞导致产权自动复归，这是地产权 (Estate) 的缺陷，而不仅仅是契约限制。
❌ 选项 C (Charitable Trust)
虽然慈善信托法（如 Cy Pres 原则）有时可以改变捐赠用途，但这需要法院判决，且具有不确定性。这种不确定性本身就使产权变得“不可售”。此外，条件是附着在土地上的，不仅仅是收益。
❌ 选项 D (Warranty)
出让人的担保仅限于他所转让的权益（即那个有缺陷的、可废止的产权）。他并没有担保这是一个绝对的完全所有权。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

1. 识别关键词： 看到 "So long as", "Until", "While" ➝ 立即反应这是 Fee Simple Determinable，伴随 Possibility of Reverter。

2. 区分阶段：
• 合同阶段 (Contract Stage)： 核心是 Marketable Title（产权是否有瑕疵）。
• 交割后阶段 (Deed Stage)： 核心是 Covenants of Title（契据中的担保）。
本题买方拒绝交割 (refused to close)，所以处于合同阶段，适用 Marketable Title 规则。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A seller and a purchaser signed a contract for the sale of a 60-year-old house. The contract required a warranty deed to be given at closing. The contract was silent regarding the condition of the house, and the purchaser did not ask. The purchaser received a warranty deed with all covenants of title at the closing and promptly recorded the deed. Approximately one month after the closing, the furnace in the house stopped working, the basement flooded, and the roof leaked so badly that the second floor could not be occupied. The seller, when told of the house's condition, was genuinely surprised.
There is no applicable statute.
The purchaser has sued the seller for damages. Will the purchaser likely be successful?

choices.A: No, because of the doctrine of merger.
choices.B: No, because the seller gave no warranty regarding the condition of the house.
choices.C: Yes, based on the covenants of title contained in the deed the purchaser received.
choices.D: Yes, because with a conveyance of residential real property, a warranty of fitness is implied.

questions.explanation:
Seller's duty to disclose
Common law (minority) rule Caveat emptor
No duty to disclose property defects unless otherwise provided
Modern (majority) rule Commercial property
Must disclose known material defects that buyer could not reasonably discover

Residential property
Exception: “as is” clause or specific disclaimers without seller's fraud

The majority of jurisdictions have enacted statutes that require sellers of residential property to disclose any known material defects that cannot be reasonably discovered by the buyer. But since there is no applicable statute in this jurisdiction, the common-law rule of caveat emptor controls. This rule (meaning “let the buyer beware”) provides that sellers have no duty to disclose property defects to the buyer unless otherwise agreed.

Here, the seller gave no warranties and the contract was silent as to the condition of the house, so the seller had no duty to disclose these defects to the buyer. Furthermore, the seller did not know about the defects in the house because she was “genuinely surprised” when she was told of the house's condition. So even if this jurisdiction had enacted a statute that followed the majority rule, the seller would not have breached any duty to disclose.

(Choice A) Under the doctrine of merger, all obligations as to title contained within the land-sale contract merge into the deed once it is delivered to and accepted by the buyer. This doctrine does not relate to issues having to do with the physical condition of the property.

(Choice C) The covenants in a warranty deed relate to the title of the property, not its physical condition.

(Choice D) A warranty of fitness or suitability† is implied in almost all jurisdictions in a contract for the sale of a newly constructed residence, so it does not apply to the sale of this 60-year-old house.

†This is also referred to as the implied warranty of quality, workmanlike construction, and habitability.

📌 Educational Objective

The common-law doctrine of caveat emptor provides that a seller has no duty to disclose property defects to the buyer unless otherwise agreed.
questions.zh-question:
一位卖方和一位买方就一栋有60年房龄的房屋签订了销售合同。合同要求在交割时提供一份保证契据。合同对房屋的状况保持沉默，买方也未曾询问。买方在交割时收到了一份包含所有产权契约的保证契据，并立即对该契据进行了登记。交割后大约一个月，房屋内的暖炉停止工作，地下室被水淹没，屋顶漏水严重以至于二楼无法居住。卖方在被告知房屋状况时，表现得十分惊讶。

本案没有适用的成文法。

买方已起诉卖方要求损害赔偿。买方是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为合并原则（doctrine of merger）。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为卖方未就房屋状况提供任何保证。
zh-choices.C: 会，基于买方收到的契据中所包含的产权契约。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为在住宅不动产的转让中，默示了适宜性保证（warranty of fitness）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property / Contracts
正确答案：B
买方不会胜诉，因为卖方未就房屋状况提供任何保证。
核心考点：买方自慎 (Caveat Emptor)

本题的核心在于普通法下的 Caveat Emptor（买方自慎）原则。

在没有成文法（Statute）特别规定的情况下，对于二手住宅（Used Residential Property）的销售：

  • 卖方对房屋的物理状况（Physical Condition）没有默示保证。
  • 除非卖方在合同中做出了明确的明示保证（Express Warranty），否则买方需自行承担房屋瑕疵的风险。

本案关键事实：
1. 合同对房屋状况保持沉默（无明示保证）。
2. 卖方对瑕疵并不知情（Genuinely surprised），因此不存在欺诈（Fraud）或隐瞒已知潜在瑕疵（Failure to disclose known latent defects）的行为。

因此，卖方没有违反任何义务，买方无法获得赔偿。

陷阱选项分析
选项 C 错误：关于保证契据 (Warranty Deed)

这是 MBE 中最常见的混淆点。Warranty Deed 中的六大契约（Covenants of Title）仅担保产权（Title）的完整性（例如：卖方确实拥有房产、房产无未披露的抵押权等），它不担保房屋的物理状况（如屋顶漏水、暖炉损坏）。

选项 D 错误：关于适宜性默示保证 (Implied Warranty of Fitness)

适宜性或宜居性默示保证（Implied Warranty of Habitability/Fitness）通常仅适用于建筑商销售的新房（New Construction）。本案中的房屋已有 60 年房龄，不适用此规则。

选项 A 错误：关于合并原则 (Doctrine of Merger)

虽然合并原则（合同条款在交割后合并入契据）是一个有效的法律概念，但它不是本案买方败诉的根本原因。买方败诉是因为从一开始就没有关于房屋状况的保证，而不是因为该保证被合并消失了。

MBE 答题技巧

遇到房屋瑕疵（Defects）问题时，请按以下步骤思考：
1. 新房还是旧房？ 新房找 Builder 可能有默示保证；旧房通常适用 Caveat Emptor。
2. 卖方是否知情？ 如果卖方知道且隐瞒（Fraud/Concealment），卖方赔；如果卖方不知情（Surprised），通常不赔。
3. 区分 Title 和 Condition： 题目提到 "Warranty Deed" 通常是想诱导你认为它包含物理质量保证，切记它只管产权！

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man owned a tract of land. His friend wanted to buy the tract and offered $20,000 for it. The man knew that the friend was insolvent but replied, "As a favor to you as an old friend, I will sell my tract to you for $20,000, even though it is worth much more, if you can raise the money within one month." The friend wrote the following words, and no more, on a piece of paper: "I agree to sell my tract to [the friend] for $20,000." The man then signed the piece of paper and gave it to the friend.
Three days later, the man received an offer of $40,000 for the tract. He asked the friend if he had raised the $20,000. When the friend answered, "Not yet," the man told him that their deal was off and that he was going to accept the $40,000 offer.
The next week, the friend secured a bank commitment to enable him to purchase the tract. The friend immediately brought an appropriate action against the man to compel the man to convey the tract to the friend.
Who will likely prevail?

choices.A: The friend, because he has equitable title.
choices.B: The friend, because the parties' antecedent agreement is enforceable.
choices.C: The man, because the man's performance was excused by the friend's anticipatory breach.
choices.D: The man, because the terms of the parties' fully integrated written agreement control.

questions.explanation:
Statute of frauds requirements for real estate contracts
Writing Physical or electronic document(s) containing reasonable basis to believe contract was formed

eg, receipt, check, emails
Signature Handwritten signature from, or other mark identifying, party to be charged

eg, letterhead, electronic signature, initials
Essential terms Typically includes:
  • identity of parties
  • words of intent to buy or sell
  • property description
  • sales price

Contracts for the sale of land are enforceable only if they comply with the statute of frauds. This statute requires that land-sale contracts be in writing, be signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought, and contain all essential terms. Essential terms often include:

  • the identity of the parties (eg, “I,” “the friend,” and the man’s signature)
  • words of intent to buy or sell (eg, “I agree to sell”)
  • a description of the property (eg, “my tract”) and
  • the sales price (eg, $20,000).

Therefore, the antecedent agreement – ie, the piece of paper on which the friend wrote “I agree to sell my tract to [the friend] for $20,000” and that the man signed – is enforceable against the man under the statute of frauds. Therefore, the friend will likely prevail.

(Choice A) The doctrine of equitable conversion relates to the ownership of property and the risk of loss in the period between contract formation and closing. However, it does not impact the validity of, or the ability to enforce, a land-sale contract.

(Choice C) Anticipatory repudiation arises when a party to a contract clearly and unequivocally expresses an unwillingness to perform. The other party may then treat that repudiation as a breach. But here, the friend’s statement that he had “not yet” raised the $20,000 expressed his willingness to perform, so no anticipatory repudiation occurred.

(Choice D) The parol evidence rule generally bars the use of extrinsic evidence of a prior or contemporaneous agreement that contradicts the written terms of a fully integrated contract. As a result, the terms of a final written agreement will control. But since the friend is able to perform under that contract, this will not help the man prevail.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the statute of frauds, a contract for the sale of land is enforceable only if it is in writing, is signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought, and contains all essential terms – ie, identifies the parties, contains words of intent to buy or sell, describes the property, and lists the sales price.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子拥有一块土地。他的朋友想购买这块土地，并出价20,000美元。该男子知道他的朋友没有偿付能力，但回答说：“看在老朋友的情分上，我愿意以20,000美元的价格将我的土地卖给你，尽管它的价值远不止于此，前提是你能在一个月内筹到这笔钱。”朋友在一张纸上写下了以下文字，仅此而已：“我同意以20,000美元的价格将我的土地卖给[朋友]。”然后，该男子在这张纸上签了字，并将其交给了朋友。

三天后，该男子收到了一个以40,000美元购买该土地的要约。他问朋友是否已经筹集到20,000美元。当朋友回答“还没有”时，该男子告诉他他们的交易取消了，他将接受那个40,000美元的要约。

接下来的一周，朋友获得了一项银行承诺，使其能够购买这块土地。朋友立即对该男子提起了适当的诉讼，要求强制该男子将土地转让给朋友。

谁可能会胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 朋友，因为他拥有衡平法上的所有权。
zh-choices.B: 朋友，因为双方的先前协议是可强制执行的。
zh-choices.C: 男子，因为朋友的预期违约免除了该男子的履行义务。
zh-choices.D: 男子，因为双方完全整合的书面协议条款具有约束力。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Estate Contracts & Statute of Frauds
正确答案：B 朋友胜诉，因为双方的先前协议（即那张纸）是可强制执行的。
核心考点：反欺诈法 (Statute of Frauds)

本题的核心在于判断那张简单的手写纸条是否构成了一份有效的、可强制执行的土地买卖合同。

根据普通法和大多数司法管辖区的规定，土地买卖合同必须满足 Statute of Frauds (SoF) 的要求才能执行。一份有效的书面文件（Memorandum）必须具备以下要素：

  • 书面形式 (Writing)： 任何形式的物理记录。
  • 基本条款 (Essential Terms)：
    ① 识别当事人 (Parties)
    ② 描述土地 (Description of Land)
    ③ 价格 (Price)
    ④ 买卖意图 (Intent to sell)
  • 签名 (Signature)： 必须由被请求执行方 (Party to be charged) 签署。

案情应用：

在本案中，朋友起诉男子（男子是被告，即 "Party to be charged"）。

  • 朋友写下的纸条包含了价格（$20,000）、当事人（“我”和朋友）、土地描述（“我的土地/my tract”）。
  • 最关键的是，男子在这张纸上签了字。

因此，这份简陋的文件满足了 Statute of Frauds 的所有要求，构成了一份具有约束力的合同。

为何男子的抗辩无效？

男子试图以“朋友还没筹到钱”为由取消合同，这涉及两个法律概念：

1. 预期违约 (Anticipatory Repudiation)

男子声称交易取消（Deal is off），但这站不住脚。预期违约要求一方明确且毫不含糊地 (unequivocally) 表示将不履行合同。

朋友只是说“还没有 (Not yet)”筹到钱，但他还有一个月的期限。在期限届满前说“还没完成”，并不代表“我不打算完成”。因此，朋友没有违约，男子的单方面解约构成了违约。

2. 完整整合协议 (Integration) - 选项D辨析

即使如选项D所述，书面协议是“完全整合”的（即排除了口头约定的“一个月期限”），这对男子也没有帮助。因为书面协议本身就是“我同意卖给你”，这是一个有效的承诺。朋友最终筹到了钱并要求履行，完全符合书面合同的条款。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

遇到“餐巾纸合同”或“便条合同”的题目时，不要因为文件看起来非正式就认为它无效。

只要检查三个要素： 1. Writing (书面) 2. Essential Terms (基本条款) 3. Signed by Defendant (被告签名)

如果满足，这就是一份铁案如山的合同 (Enforceable Contract)。
MBE Property Law Review

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A seller owned a house situated on a two-acre lot in an area zoned for single-family residential uses only. Although it was not discernible from the outside, the house had been converted by the seller from a single-family house to a structure that contained three separate apartments, in violation of the zoning ordinance. The conversion was also in violation of the building code.
The seller and a buyer entered into a valid written contract for the purchase and sale of the house. The contract provided that the seller was to convey to the buyer marketable title. The contract was silent as to zoning. The buyer then fully inspected the house.
Prior to the closing, the buyer learned that the house did not conform to the zoning ordinance and refused to close although the seller was ready, willing, and able to perform his contract obligations. The seller brought an appropriate action for specific performance against the buyer.
Is the seller likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the illegal conversion of the house creates the risk of litigation.
choices.B: No, because the illegal conversion of the house was done by the seller rather than by a predecessor.
choices.C: Yes, because the buyer was charged with knowledge of the zoning ordinance prior to entering the contract.
choices.D: Yes, because the seller was able to convey a marketable title.

questions.explanation:
"Red flags" for marketable title

  • Covenants
  • Easements
  • Leases
  • Liens
  • Gaps in chain of title
  • Boundary disputes
  • Existing zoning violations
  • Adverse possession

The warranty of marketable title is implied in all real estate contracts unless otherwise provided. This guarantees that, upon closing, the seller will convey the buyer title that is reasonably free from doubt and under no threat of litigation such that a reasonable person would accept and pay for it. This does not mean that title must be free from any defect, but it should ensure peaceable and quiet enjoyment of the property.

An existing violation of a zoning ordinance exposes the real estate owner to potential litigation, so such a violation renders title unmarketable.* This means that the seller's illegal conversion of the house in violation of the zoning ordinance prevents him from delivering marketable title to the buyer (Choice D). Therefore, his action for specific performance to compel the buyer to purchase the house will likely fail.

*While existing zoning violations render title unmarketable, courts have consistently held that existing building code violations do not.

(Choice B) The illegal conversion of the house renders title unmarketable regardless of whether the seller or a predecessor did the conversion.

(Choice C) Although the buyer was charged with knowledge of the zoning ordinance prior to entering the contract, the buyer was not charged with knowing whether the house complied with that ordinance. Instead, the buyer could rely on the implied warranty of marketability in the land-sale contract and inspect the property for noncompliance prior to closing.

📌 Educational Objective

Marketable title exists when title is reasonably free from doubt and under no threat of litigation such that a reasonable person would accept and pay for it. Therefore, an existing zoning violation renders title unmarketable.

📚 References
  • 77 Am. Jur. 2d Vendor and Purchaser § 93 (2020) (defining marketable title).

一位卖方拥有一栋房屋，该房屋坐落于一块两英亩的土地上，该区域被划定为仅限单户住宅用途。尽管从外部无法辨别，但该房屋已被卖方从单户住宅改建为一个包含三个独立公寓的建筑，这违反了区域规划条例。该改建也违反了建筑法规。

卖方和一位买方就该房屋的买卖签订了一份有效的书面合同。合同规定，卖方应向买方转让可售卖的产权（marketable title）。合同对区域规划问题未作规定。随后，买方对房屋进行了全面检查。

在过户前，买方了解到该房屋不符合区域规划条例，因此拒绝完成交易，尽管所有权人已经准备好、愿意且能够履行其合同义务。所有权人对买方提起了要求强制履行（specific performance）的适当诉讼。

该所有权人是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为房屋的非法改建带来了诉讼风险。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为房屋的非法改建是由该所有权人而非前手所为。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为在签订合同前，买方被推定知晓区域规划条例。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该所有权人能够转让可售卖的产权（marketable title）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property / Marketable Title
正确答案
选项 A
不会胜诉，因为房屋的非法改建带来了诉讼风险。
核心考点：可售卖产权 (Marketable Title)

在每一份土地买卖合同中，除非另有约定，卖方都默示担保提供Marketable Title。

定义：
可售卖产权是指不存在合理疑点（reasonably free from doubt）且没有诉讼威胁（threat of litigation）的产权。

如果产权存在使买方在过户后面临被起诉风险的瑕疵，该产权即为“不可售卖”（Unmarketable）。买方有权拒绝过户（Closing）。

关键区分：规划限制 vs. 规划违规

这是MBE考试中极易混淆的考点，请务必区分：

情况 对产权适销性的影响
Zoning Restrictions
(仅存在规划条例本身)
例：该地块被划定为仅限单户住宅。 		✅ 不影响
产权仍是 Marketable 的。买方必须接受土地受法律管辖的事实。
Existing Zoning Violation
(现存的违规行为)
例：在单户住宅区建了三户公寓。 		❌ 导致 Unmarketable
因为政府可能起诉买方，要求拆除或罚款。这构成了诉讼风险。
本案逻辑推演
  1. 现状：卖方将单户住宅改建为三户公寓，违反了 Zoning Ordinance。
  2. 后果：这属于 Existing Zoning Violation。
  3. 法律效力：这种违规行为使买方面临被政府强制执行（如强制拆除改建部分）的诉讼风险。
  4. 结论：产权是 Unmarketable 的。
  5. 结果：卖方无法提供合同要求的产权，因此无法强制买方履行合同（Specific Performance）。
为什么其他选项是错的？
  • 选项 B (前手行为)： 错误。产权是否有瑕疵看的是“现状”。无论是谁造成的违规，只要违规存在，买方就面临风险。
  • 选项 C (买方知情)： 错误。买方被推定知晓“法律”（即该地有规划条例），但不被推定知晓“事实”（即房屋违反了该条例）。买方有权依赖卖方的默示担保。
  • 关于建筑法规 (Building Code)： 题目虽然提到也违反了建筑法规，但在MBE中，通常只有违反Zoning才直接导致产权不可售卖；单纯违反建筑法规（如电线布线错误）通常不影响产权适销性，除非合同另有规定。但本题中Zoning违规是决定性因素。
MBE Real Property Review © 2025
Focus: Marketable Title & Zoning

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A seller owns a 400-acre tract of land with 5,000 feet of frontage on a county highway. The seller and a buyer entered into a written agreement for the sale of a portion of the tract identified only as "a parcel of land, containing not less than 100 acres and having not less than 1,000 feet of frontage on the county highway, whose exact location and dimensions are to be determined by the parties hereto, at a price of $8,000 per acre."
Shortly after the execution of the agreement, the parties met to stake out the parcel of land to be sold, but they could not agree. The disagreement intensified, and the seller repudiated the contract.
The buyer has sued the seller for specific performance. The seller has asserted all available defenses.
Is the buyer entitled to specific performance of the contract?

choices.A: No, because a contract for the sale of real property that requires further agreement on an essential element cannot be specifically enforced.
choices.B: No, because the purchase price was not fixed by, nor determinable under, the contract terms.
choices.C: Yes, because the contract bound the parties to act in good faith and to agree upon the specific land to be conveyed.
choices.D: Yes, because the equity powers of the court enable the court to appoint a master, or to take other appropriate action, to identify the land to be conveyed.

questions.explanation:
Essential terms for real estate contracts
Identify parties
Words of intent
…to buy and to sell…
Property description
303
304
305
306
307
308
Sales price
$ $ $

Under the statute of frauds, contracts for the sale of land (ie, real estate contracts) are enforceable only if they are in writing, are signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought, and contain all essential terms. Essential terms include:

  • the identity of the parties
  • words of intent to buy or sell
  • a description of the property and
  • the sales price.

Although courts may liberally construe the property-description requirement, the writing must contain some evidence of the specific property to be sold. Here, the writing expressly stated that the parties had yet to agree on what land was to be conveyed. Therefore, the statute of frauds makes the contract unenforceable.

(Choice B) The sales price is also an essential term. It can be listed in gross (eg, at a set price) or determined by the actual quantity of land sold (eg, at a per-acre price). Therefore, the agreement to purchase the land “at a price of $8,000 per acre” satisfies this requirement.

(Choices C & D) The statute of frauds requires that a contract for the sale of land identify the land to be sold. Good faith and equity cannot provide relief for this omission.

📌 Educational Objective

The statute of frauds requires that land-sale contracts contain all essential terms—ie, the identity of the parties, words of intent to buy or sell, a description of the property, and the sales price.

📚 References
  • 73 Am. Jur. 2d Statute of Frauds §§ 289, 305, 325, 329 (2020).
questions.zh-question:
一名卖方拥有一片400英亩的土地，该土地有5000英尺的临郡公路路段。卖方与一名买方签订了一份书面协议，出售该片土地的一部分，该部分土地仅被描述为“一块土地，面积不小于100英亩，临郡公路路段不小于1000英尺，其确切位置和尺寸将由本协议双方决定，价格为每英亩8000美元。”

协议签订后不久，双方会面以确定待售土地的界限，但未能达成一致。分歧加剧，卖方拒绝履行合同。

买方已起诉卖方，要求强制履行。卖方已提出所有可用的抗辩。

买方是否有权要求强制履行该合同？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为一份要求就某一基本要素进行进一步协商的不动产销售合同，不能被强制履行。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为购买价格既没有在合同中固定，也无法根据合同条款确定。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为合同约束双方本着善意行事，并就待转让的具体土地达成一致。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为法院的衡平法权力使其能够指定一名主事官，或采取其他适当行动，以确定待转让的土地。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

不动产合同与防止欺诈法
核心法律规则：防止欺诈法

根据防止欺诈法 (Statute of Frauds, SOF)，土地销售合同必须满足以下条件才具有可执行性：

  • 必须是书面形式 (in writing)；
  • 由被执行方签署 (signed by the party to be charged)；
  • 包含所有基本条款 (essential terms)。
为什么本案合同不可执行？

1. 财产描述是基本条款

在不动产合同中，"基本条款"必须包括对财产的充分描述 (sufficient description of the property)。法院需要能够根据合同内容明确辨认出具体要转让哪一块土地。

2. "协议达成一致" (Agreement to Agree) 的陷阱

本案中，合同虽然规定了面积（100英亩）和临路长度（1000英尺），但明确写道：

"确切位置和尺寸将由本协议双方决定" (exact location and dimensions are to be determined by the parties)

这被称为"Agreement to Agree"（即约定未来再达成协议）。由于双方未能就这一核心要素达成一致，法院无法代替双方做出决定。法院无法强制执行一个连标的物都不确定的合同。

结论：由于缺少对土地的具体描述这一基本条款，合同不满足防止欺诈法的要求，因此买方无法获得强制履行 (Specific Performance) 的救济。

干扰项辨析
❌ 选项 B (关于价格)：
虽然价格也是基本条款，但它不需要是一个具体的总数字。只要价格是可确定的 (determinable) 即可。本案中 "$8,000 per acre" 结合具体的英亩数是可以算出价格的，因此价格条款本身没有问题。
❌ 选项 C & D (关于善意与衡平法)：
虽然合同法强调善意 (good faith)，衡平法 (equity) 也有补救功能，但它们不能用来修补防止欺诈法所要求的核心书面要素的缺失。如果合同根本没有确定卖哪块地，法院不能凭空"创造"一个合同来执行。
MBE 答题技巧

在处理不动产合同题目时，如果看到"从大块土地中出售一部分"的情节，立即检查合同是否明确界定了这部分土地的位置。

如果合同说"位置由双方日后商定"且双方后来闹翻了，这通常意味着合同因缺乏基本条款（描述不详）而不可执行。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A seller had promised a buyer that, if at any time the seller decided to sell his summer cottage property, he would give the buyer the opportunity to purchase the cottage.
At a time when the buyer was serving overseas with the United States Navy, the seller decided to sell the cottage for $200,000 and spoke to the buyer's mother. Before the buyer sailed, he had arranged for the mother to become a joint owner of his various bank accounts so that the mother would be able to pay his bills when he was gone. When she heard from the seller, the mother took the necessary funds from the buyer's account and paid the seller $200,000. Two weeks later, the seller executed and delivered to the mother a deed in the proper form purporting to convey the cottage to the buyer. The mother promptly and properly recorded the deed.
Shortly thereafter, the mother learned that the buyer had been killed in an accident at sea one week before the delivery of the deed. The buyer's last will, which has now been duly probated, leaves his entire estate to his church. The mother is the sole heir-at-law of the buyer.
There is no statute dealing with conveyances to dead persons.
Who has title to the cottage?

choices.A: The church.
choices.B: The mother.
choices.C: The seller.
choices.D: The seller, subject to a lien to secure $200,000 to the buyer's estate.

questions.explanation:
Seller gives Buyer option to buy cottage
→
Mother exercises option by paying $200,000
↓
Buyer acquires equitable title
→
Buyer dies & leaves estate to church
↓
Church receives equitable title
→
Seller delivers deed at closing
↓
Church gains full ownership (equitable & legal title)

Although the buyer left his entire estate to the church, the cottage would only be part of that estate if the buyer had an interest in the cottage when he died. He did not have legal title upon death since the seller had not yet delivered the deed. But under the doctrine of equitable conversion, the buyer did have equitable title — ie, the right to obtain full ownership of the property (ie, legal and equitable title) upon closing. That is because an enforceable sales contract was formed when the buyer's mother exercised the option to buy the cottage on his behalf.

Since equitable title is a real property interest, it passed to the church under the buyer's will. The church then obtained legal title to, and full ownership of, the cottage upon closing — when the seller delivered the deed to the mother (Choices B & C).

(Choice D) If a buyer conveys his/her equitable title before the purchase price has been paid, that title will be subject to the seller's equitable lien. But here, the mother paid the purchase price ($200,000) before the cottage was devised to the church. Therefore, the seller has no lien on the church's title or any other interest in the cottage.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the doctrine of equitable conversion, a purchaser receives equitable title to property when he/she enters an enforceable sales contract (eg, by paying the sale price). Equitable title is a real property interest that gives the purchaser the right to obtain full ownership of the property upon closing (eg, when the seller delivers the deed).

📚 References
  • 77 Am. Jur. 2d Vendor and Purchaser § 26 (2018) (option contract).

卖方曾向买方承诺，如果卖方在任何时候决定出售其避暑小屋的房产，他将给予买方购买该小屋的机会。

在买方于 United States Navy 海外服役期间，卖方决定以20万美元的价格出售该小屋，并与买方的母亲进行了交谈。在买方出海前，他已安排其母亲成为他多个银行账户的共同所有人，以便在他离开期间，母亲能够支付他的账单。当她从卖方处得知消息后，母亲从买方的账户中取出所需资金，并向卖方支付了20万美元。两周后，卖方签署并向母亲交付了一份格式正确的地契，意图将小屋转让给买方。母亲及时并妥善地登记了该地契。

此后不久，母亲得知买方在地契交付一周前于一次海上事故中丧生。买方的最终遗嘱现已经过正式认证，将其全部遗产留给了他的教会。母亲是买方的唯一法定继承人。

没有处理向死者转让财产的成文法。

谁拥有该小屋的产权？

zh-choices.A: 教会。
zh-choices.B: 母亲。
zh-choices.C: 卖方。
zh-choices.D: 卖方，但其产权附带一项为买方遗产担保20万美元的留置权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Equitable Conversion

💡 核心原则：衡平法转换 (Equitable Conversion)

一旦签订了可强制执行的不动产买卖合同（enforceable contract），买方在衡平法上即被视为土地的所有者（拥有 Equitable Title），而卖方仅保留法定所有权（Legal Title）作为收取价款的担保。

📅 案件时间线梳理
第一阶段
合同成立 (Contract Formed)
母亲代表买方支付 $200,000。
👉 此时买方获得 Equitable Title。
第二阶段
买方去世 (Buyer Dies)
买方在海上事故中丧生。
👉 其 Equitable Title 作为不动产权益进入遗产。
第三阶段
地契交付 (Deed Delivered)
卖方将地契交给母亲。
👉 此时完成 Legal Title 的转移。
⚖️ 法律逻辑推演

1. 为什么合同有效？
卖方提供了购买机会，母亲作为买方的代理人（通过共同账户授权）支付了全款。这一行为构成了对卖方要约的承诺（Acceptance），形成了可强制执行的合同。

2. 衡平法转换 (Equitable Conversion) 的效力
在合同成立的那一刻，根据衡平法转换原则，买方（Buyer）成为了房屋的衡平法所有人 (Equitable Owner)。这种权益属于不动产 (Real Property)。

3. 死亡与遗嘱 (Death & Will)
买方去世时，他拥有该房屋的衡平法产权。根据他的遗嘱（Will），所有遗产（entire estate）都留给了教会。因此，教会继承了这部分不动产权益。

4. 谁拥有最终产权？
由于购房款已经全额支付，卖方不再拥有任何权益（连担保权都没有了）。虽然地契是在买方死后交付的（普通法下向死者交付地契通常无效），但这不影响教会已经通过遗嘱继承了衡平法上的所有权。教会作为衡平法所有人，有权要求获得法定产权（Legal Title）。因此，在实质上，教会拥有该小屋。

❌ 干扰项排除
A. 教会 (The Church)
正确。买方的衡平法产权属于不动产，根据遗嘱条款，由教会继承。
B. 母亲 (The Mother)
错误。母亲是法定继承人（Heir-at-law），但当存在有效遗嘱时，遗嘱优先于法定继承。买方的遗嘱将所有财产留给了教会。
C. 卖方 (The Seller)
错误。卖方已经收到了全款，合同已履行。卖方仅持有“裸法定产权”(Bare Legal Title)，且必须为了衡平法所有人的利益持有。
D. 卖方带留置权
错误。卖方的留置权（Vendor's Lien）仅在买方未付清款项时存在。本案中，母亲已支付了 $200,000 全款，因此不存在留置权。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
When a buyer and a seller executed a valid contract for the sale of a house, the buyer gave the seller $1,000 as earnest money. The contract noted that the earnest money tendered would be applied to the purchase price at the time of sale but was silent as to remedies in the event of any default.
Just before the closing, the buyer lost her job. The buyer told the seller that she could no longer purchase the house and asked him to return the earnest money. The seller accurately told the buyer that the seller's actual losses exceeded the amount of the earnest money; that if the seller sued the buyer for damages, he would receive a minimum of $5,000; and that it would be difficult for him to sell the house in the current market.
Should the buyer get the earnest money back?

choices.A: No, because the contract was silent regarding remedies.
choices.B: No, because the seller's actual losses exceeded the amount of the earnest money.
choices.C: Yes, because the buyer is no longer ready, willing, and able to purchase the house.
choices.D: Yes, because the reason for the buyer's default was not anticipated.

questions.explanation:
Seller's remedies
Rescission & restitution
  • Rescind (ie, cancel) agreement & recover possession of property
  • Rental value & physical damages are recoverable
  • Buyer not liable for purchase price
Specific performance
  • Seek an injunction ordering buyer to pay agreed purchase price
  • May be unavailable if money damages provide adequate compensation & property is not unique
    • eg, condominium identical to other units in complex
Damages
  • Loss of bargain = contract price – market value at time of breach
  • Liquidated damages = amount designated in the sales contract as compensation for breach
  • Retain buyer's deposit (up to amount of seller's actual damages)
  • Incidental & consequential damages that were contemplated during sales contract or reasonably foreseeable

Earnest money is a deposit paid by a buyer to show a good-faith intent to complete the transaction. Once accepted, the seller cannot recover other damages for breach. That is because earnest money typically constitutes liquidated damages—ie, an amount agreed upon during good-faith negotiations to reasonably compensate the injured party. These damages are recoverable unless they constitute a penalty (eg, when liquidated damages far exceed actual damages). In such a case, the seller can only recover actual damages.

Here, the buyer gave the seller $1,000 as earnest money. The contract was silent as to remedies, so the $1,000 constitutes liquidated damages (Choice A). The buyer breached the contract when she reported that she could no longer purchase the house, causing the seller to sustain losses. Since those actual losses exceed the amount of the earnest money, the liquidated damages provision is likely enforceable. As a result, the seller should receive the full $1,000 and the buyer should not receive any earnest money back.

(Choice C) The seller is entitled to the $1,000 because the buyer is no longer ready, willing, and able to purchase the house. This fact would not allow the buyer to get the earnest money back.

(Choice D) Unless otherwise stated, liquidated damages will be paid to the injured party as compensation for any breach, regardless of whether the breach was anticipated.

📌 Educational Objective

Earnest money typically constitutes liquidated damages, which are generally recoverable upon the buyer's breach. But if liquidated damages are deemed a penalty (eg, when they far exceed actual damages), then the seller may recover only actual damages.

📚 References
  • 22 Am. Jur. 2d Damages § 540 (2020) (earnest deposit considered liquidated damages).
  • 77 Am. Jur. 2d Vendor and Purchaser § 478 (2020) (seller's recovery of liquidated damages).
questions.zh-question:
当买卖双方就一栋房屋的销售签订了一份有效合同后，买方支付给卖方1000美元作为定金。合同注明，所付定金将在销售时用于抵扣购买价格，但对于任何违约情况下的救济措施保持沉默。

就在过户前，买方失去了工作。买方告诉卖方她无法再购买该房屋，并要求卖方退还定金。卖方如实告知买方，卖方的实际损失超过了定金的数额；如果卖方起诉买方要求损害赔偿，他将至少获得5000美元；并且在当前市场上他很难卖掉这栋房子。

买方是否应该拿回定金？

zh-choices.A: 不应该，因为合同对救济措施保持沉默。
zh-choices.B: 不应该，因为卖方的实际损失超过了定金的数额。
zh-choices.C: 应该，因为买方已不再准备好、愿意且能够购买该房屋。
zh-choices.D: 应该，因为买方违约的原因是未曾预料到的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：不动产定金与违约救济

本题考察的是不动产买卖合同中，当买方违约（Breach of Contract）时，卖方是否有权保留定金（Earnest Money）。

核心法律规则：
在没有明确违约金条款的情况下，如果买方无正当理由违约，卖方通常有权保留定金，前提是定金金额合理且不超过卖方的实际损失（Actual Damages）。

1. 法律分析：为什么选 B？

正确答案是 B。

逻辑推演如下：

  • 定金的性质： 定金（Earnest Money）通常被视为一种预设的约定违约金（Liquidated Damages）。它的目的是在买方违约时补偿卖方。
  • 合同的沉默： 即使合同没有明确说明违约救济措施，法院通常也允许卖方在买方违约时保留定金。
  • 关键测试——罚金原则（Penalty Doctrine）： 约定违约金必须是合理的，不能具有惩罚性。如果定金数额巨大，而卖方实际损失很小，法院可能会判定没收定金是不公平的“罚金”。
  • 本案事实： 卖方的实际损失（超过$5,000）远大于定金（$1,000）。因此，卖方保留这$1,000完全是用于弥补实际损失，不存在不当得利（Unjust Enrichment）或惩罚性过高的问题。

因此，因为卖方遭受了实质性的经济损失，且该损失超过了定金金额，卖方有权保留定金。

2. 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (错误)：
“因为合同对救济措施保持沉默。”
虽然合同沉默，但这并不是卖方能保留定金的根本原因。如果卖方没有任何损失却没收了定金，法院可能会要求退还部分定金以防止不当得利。卖方能保留定金的核心原因是存在实际损失。

选项 C (错误)：
“因为买方不再准备好、愿意且能够购买。”
这是买方违约的事实描述，但这本身并不自动决定定金的归属。如果定金数额极高（例如房价的50%），即使买方违约，法院也可能判决退还部分定金。关键在于损害赔偿的合理性。

选项 D (错误)：
“因为违约原因是未曾预料到的。”
买方失业（Financial Inability）虽然是不幸的，但在合同法中通常不构成履约不能（Impossibility）或商业目的落空（Frustration of Purpose）的有效抗辩。买方的个人财务状况变化风险通常由买方自己承担，这不能成为要求退还定金的理由。

🎓 MBE 破题金钥匙

在处理不动产违约金问题时，请遵循以下步骤：

  1. 确定违约方： 谁搞砸了交易？（本题是买方）。
  2. 检查定金金额： 通常定金占房价的 10% 或更少被视为合理的约定违约金（Liquidated Damages）。
  3. 比较损失：
    • 如果 定金 ≈ 实际损失 ➡️ 卖方保留。
    • 如果 定金 < 实际损失 ➡️ 卖方保留（甚至可能起诉追讨更多，除非合同限制了救济）。
    • 如果 定金 >>> 实际损失 ➡️ 买方可能拿回差额（避免罚金性质）。

本题中，实际损失 > 定金，这是最强有力的理由支持卖方保留款项。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
Six months ago, a man told his cousin that he would give her his farm as a gift on her next birthday. The cousin then entered into a valid written contract to sell the farm to an investor with the closing to take place "one week after [the cousin's] next birthday."
The man failed to convey the farm to the cousin on her birthday. One week after the cousin's birthday, on the intended closing date, the investor first learned of the cousin's inability to convey the farm because the man had breached his promise. The investor considered suing the cousin but realized that the cousin could not be compelled to convey the farm because it was still owned by the man.
Two weeks after the cousin's birthday, the man died. Under his valid will, the man devised the farm to the cousin. Within a week, the executor of the man's estate gave the cousin an executor's deed to the farm in compliance with state law. The investor promptly learned of this transfer and demanded that the cousin convey the farm to her. The cousin refused.
The investor sued the cousin for specific performance.
Who will likely prevail?

choices.A: The cousin, because she received title by devise rather than by conveyance.
choices.B: The cousin, because the contract to convey was not signed by the legal owner of the farm as of the date of the contract and was therefore void.
choices.C: The investor, because the contract to convey merged into the executor's deed to the cousin.
choices.D: The investor, because the contract to convey remained enforceable by her within a reasonable period of time after the proposed closing date.

questions.explanation:
Timeline for sale of real estate

Property placed on market
Buyer offers to purchase
Seller accepts
(sales contract formed)
Closing
(transaction complete)
Listing period
Executory period

The sale of real property typically comprises three parts:

  • Execution of the sales contract – the buyer promises to pay the purchase price in exchange for the seller's promise to deliver title
  • Executory period – the buyer can inspect the property, secure a loan, and review title documents; the seller can repair the property or correct imperfections in the title
  • Closing – the seller formally transfers title by delivering the deed to the buyer; the buyer pays the purchase price

A closing date is not an essential term of a land-sale contract, so the seller's performance is due at or within a reasonable time after the closing date unless time is of the essence. Time is of the essence when the contract or circumstances strongly suggest that the parties intended that the closing date be strictly enforced – not the case here. Therefore, the contract between the cousin and the investor was still enforceable when the cousin acquired title to the farm shortly after the proposed closing date, and the investor will likely prevail.

(Choice A) Since the cousin acquired title within a reasonable time after the proposed closing date, she was contractually obligated to transfer title to the investor. The method through which she received title (by devise or conveyance) is irrelevant.

(Choice B) The seller need not have title at the time the land-sale contract is executed since performance is not due until closing. As a result, the cousin could sign the contract with the investor even though she was not the legal owner of the farm at that time.

(Choice C) Under the merger rule, a land-sale contract merges into the deed of conveyance at the time of closing, so only the guarantees reflected in the deed remain. This means that the contract will merge into the cousin's deed (not the executor's deed) once the deed is conveyed.

📌 Educational Objective

A seller need not transfer title until closing or a reasonable time thereafter unless time is of the essence – ie, if the contract or circumstances strongly suggest that the parties intended the closing date to be strictly enforced.
questions.zh-question:
六个月前，一名男子告诉他的表亲，他将在她下一个生日时将他的农场作为礼物赠予她。该表亲随后与一名投资者签订了一份有效的书面合同，将该农场出售给该投资者，并约定交割将在“[该表亲]下一个生日后一周”进行。

该男子未能在表亲生日当天将农场转让给她。表亲生日后一周，即预定的交割日，投资者才得知由于该男子违背其承诺，导致表亲无法转让该农场。投资者考虑起诉该表亲，但意识到由于农场仍为该男子所有，无法强制表亲转让农场。

表亲生日后两周，该男子去世。根据其有效遗嘱，该男子将农场遗赠给了表亲。一周内，该男子遗产的执行人根据州法律，将农场的执行人契约交给了表亲。投资者迅速得知此项转让，并要求表亲将农场转让给她。表亲拒绝了。

投资者起诉表亲，要求其进行特定履行（specific performance）。

谁可能会胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 表亲，因为她是通过遗赠而非转让获得所有权的。
zh-choices.B: 表亲，因为转让合同在签订之日并非由农场的合法所有人签署，因此该合同无效。
zh-choices.C: 投资者，因为转让合同已并入授予表亲的执行人契约中。
zh-choices.D: 投资者，因为在拟议的交割日期后的合理期限内，她仍然可以强制执行该转让合同。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

Real Estate Contracts
正确答案：D 投资者胜诉，因为在拟议的交割日期后的合理期限内，她仍然可以强制执行该转让合同。
⚖️ 核心法律规则

本题主要考察不动产买卖合同中的两个关键概念：

  1. 履行时间 (Time of Performance)：除非合同明确规定或情况表明Time is of the essence（时间至关重要），否则交割日期并非绝对截止日。
  2. 产权交付能力 (Ability to Convey Title)：卖方只需在交割时（Closing）拥有产权，而无需在签约时拥有。
🔍 深度解析

1. 时间并非至关重要 (Time is NOT of the Essence)

在普通法和大多数司法管辖区，土地销售合同中的交割日期被视为目标日期。除非合同中有明确条款说明“时间至关重要”，或者周围环境强烈暗示这一点，否则一方在交割日期的延迟履行并不构成实质性违约（Material Breach）。

在本案中，虽然表亲未能在原定日期交割，但合同并未规定时间至关重要。因此，表亲有权在原定日期后的合理时间 (Reasonable Time)内完成履约。

2. 延迟后的履行能力

表亲在原定交割日后仅两周（通过遗嘱）获得了农场的所有权，并在一周后拿到了契约。这通常被视为在“合理时间”范围内。一旦她获得了产权，她就有能力履行合同。由于合同仍然有效（未因轻微延迟而终止），投资者有权要求Specific Performance（特定履行/强制履行）。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 A 错误： 获得产权的方式无关紧要。 无论是通过赠与（Conveyance）还是遗赠（Devise）获得产权，只要卖方拥有了合法的Marketable Title（适销产权），她就有义务履行出售合同。
选项 B 错误： 签约时无需拥有产权。 这是MBE常见的陷阱。法律允许人们出售他们尚未拥有的东西，只要他们在交割时 (Closing) 能够交付产权即可。因此，合同自始有效。
选项 C 错误： 合并原则 (Merger Doctrine) 适用对象错误。 合并原则是指土地销售合同的条款会并入最终交付给买方的契约（Deed）中。本案中，执行人给表亲的契约与投资者无关；投资者尚未收到契约，因此合同尚未“合并”消失，投资者仍可依据合同起诉。

遇到“卖方无产权”题目时的思考步骤：

  • 第一步：看签约时？（无产权不影响合同有效性）。
  • 第二步：看交割时？（卖方必须在交割时提供产权）。
  • 第三步：看是否迟延？（若非 Time is of the essence，卖方有合理宽限期去搞定产权）。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
The owner of a tract of land mortgaged the tract to a bank to secure his preexisting obligation to the bank. The mortgage was promptly and properly recorded. The owner and a buyer then entered into a valid written contract for the purchase and sale of the tract, which provided for the transfer of "a marketable title, free of encumbrances." The contract did not expressly refer to the mortgage.
Shortly after entering into the contract, the buyer found another property that much better suited her needs and decided to try to avoid her contract with the owner. When the buyer discovered the existence of the mortgage, she asserted that the title was encumbered and that she would not close. The owner responded by offering to provide for payment and discharge of the mortgage at the closing from the proceeds of the closing. The buyer refused to go forward, and the owner brought an appropriate action against her for specific performance.
If the court holds for the owner in this action, what would be the likely reason?

choices.A: The doctrine of equitable conversion supports the result.
choices.B: The existence of the mortgage was not the buyer's real reason for refusing to close.
choices.C: The mortgage is not entitled to priority because it was granted for preexisting obligations.
choices.D: The owner's arrangements for the payment of the mortgage fully satisfied his obligation to deliver marketable title.

questions.explanation:
"Red flags" for marketable title
  • Covenants
  • Easements
  • Leases
  • Liens
  • Gaps in chain of title
  • Boundary disputes
  • Existing zoning violations
  • Adverse possession

All contracts for the sale of land have an implied warranty that the seller will convey marketable title to the buyer upon closing unless otherwise stated. Title need not be perfect to be marketable. However, it must be reasonably free from doubt and under no threat of litigation such that a reasonable person would accept and pay for it. If the seller cannot convey marketable title by the time of closing, the buyer can rescind (ie, cancel) the contract.

Title can be rendered unmarketable by encumbrances (eg, easements, mortgages, other liens). Although a mortgage is an encumbrance, the seller has the right to satisfy the mortgage up to the time of closing and will often use the sale proceeds to do so — as the owner has made arrangements to do here. As a result, the court will hold for the owner because the closing itself will likely render title marketable.

(Choice A) The doctrine of equitable conversion relates to the ownership of the property and the risk of loss in the period between contract formation and closing. It does not affect the parties' performance under the land-sale contract.

(Choice B) The buyer could have refused to close if she had an actual basis for doing so — even if that was not the buyer's actual reason for the refusal.

(Choice C) Priority refers to the order in which creditors receive sale proceeds from a foreclosure; whether a mortgage was granted for preexisting obligations does not affect its priority. Regardless, this will not affect the owner's success because (1) there is no indication that there are other encumbrances on the property, and (2) the mortgage will likely be satisfied and thereby extinguished upon closing.

📌 Educational Objective

A mortgage is an encumbrance that can render title unmarketable. However, the seller has the right to satisfy the mortgage up to the time of closing and will often use the sale proceeds to do so.
questions.zh-question:
一块土地的所有人将该土地抵押给一家银行，以担保其对银行已有的债务。该抵押被及时且适当地进行了登记。随后，该所有人和一名买方签订了一份有效的书面买卖合同，合同规定转让“无产权负担的可售卖所有权”。合同中并未明确提及该抵押。

签订合同后不久，买方发现了另一处更适合她需求的房产，并决定试图避免履行与所有人的合同。当买方发现该抵押的存在时，她主张该所有权存在产权负担，并表示她不会完成交易。所有人回应称，他将在交易完成时，用交易所得款项支付并清偿该抵押。买方拒绝继续进行交易，所有人对她提起了要求强制履行的适当诉讼。

如果法院在此诉讼中支持了所有人，最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 衡平法转换原则 (equitable conversion) 支持此判决结果。
zh-choices.B: 抵押的存在并非买方拒绝完成交易的真实原因。
zh-choices.C: 该抵押不享有优先权，因为它是为已有的债务而设定的。
zh-choices.D: 所有人为支付抵押所做的安排，完全履行了他交付可售卖所有权的义务。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Marketable Title
正确答案：D 所有人为支付抵押所做的安排，完全履行了他交付可售卖所有权的义务。
核心考点：可售卖所有权 (Marketable Title)

在土地买卖合同中，卖方有一项默示担保 (Implied Warranty)，即在交易完成时 (at closing) 提供可售卖所有权。

什么是可售卖所有权？
并非完美无瑕的所有权，而是指一个理性买家愿意接受、没有重大诉讼风险的所有权。

关键规则：同步清偿 (Simultaneous Satisfaction)

虽然抵押 (Mortgage) 确实是一种产权负担 (Encumbrance)，通常会使所有权不可售卖，但法律允许卖方利用“时间差”进行补救：

合同签订时
土地上存在抵押，此时所有权有负担。
交易完成日 (Closing Day)
卖方有权使用买方支付的购房款 (Proceeds) 当场清偿抵押。
结果
只要卖方安排了在 Closing 时还款，所有权在交付的那一刻就是“干净”的。

因此，买方不能以“存在抵押”为借口在 Closing 之前拒绝履行合同，除非卖方明显无力偿还（例如抵押金额高于房价）。

干扰项分析
A 错误 衡平法转换 (Equitable Conversion)： 该原则主要涉及签约后、过户前房屋毁损的风险承担问题（Risk of Loss），与卖方是否有能力提供好标题无关。
B 错误 买方的真实动机： 虽然买方确实是想找借口毁约，但如果所有权真的不可售卖，买方的动机就不重要了（她有权合法退出）。她败诉的原因不是因为她动机不纯，而是因为卖方确实提供了合格的所有权。
C 错误 抵押的优先权 (Priority)： 抵押权是否针对“已有债务”设定，只影响债权人之间的受偿顺序，不影响该抵押权作为产权负担的性质。只要它存在，就需要被清除，而卖方已经安排了清除。
💡 MBE 考试技巧
看到“买方因发现抵押想毁约”的题目时，首先检查：
卖方是否打算用出售所得款 (Proceeds) 在 Closing 时还贷？
如果是，买方通常不能以此为由拒绝交易。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A seller entered into a written contract to sell a tract of land to an investor. The contract made no mention of the quality of title to be conveyed. The seller and the investor later completed the sale, and the seller delivered a warranty deed to the investor.
Soon thereafter, the value of the land increased dramatically. The investor entered into a written contract to sell the land to a buyer. The contract between the investor and the buyer expressly provided that the investor would convey a marketable title. The buyer's attorney discovered that the title to the land was not marketable and had not been marketable when the original seller had conveyed to the investor. The buyer refused to complete the sale.
The investor sued the original seller for breach of contract, claiming damages from the seller's failure to convey marketable title, which resulted in the investor's loss of the sale to the subsequent buyer.
Who is likely to prevail on this count?

choices.A: The investor, because the law implies in such a contract a covenant that the title will be marketable.
choices.B: The investor, because the original seller is liable for all reasonably foreseeable damages.
choices.C: The original seller, because her contract obligations as to title merged into the deed.
choices.D: The original seller, because she did not expressly agree to convey marketable title.

questions.explanation:
All contracts for the sale of land, unless otherwise stated, impliedly warrant that the seller will convey marketable title to the buyer upon closing (Choices A & D). However, once a deed is delivered to and accepted by the buyer, the doctrine of merger provides that all obligations contained within the land-sale contract merge into the deed. Those obligations can be enforced thereafter only if they are incorporated into the deed.

Here, the investor has sued the original seller for breach of contract, claiming damages from the seller's failure to convey marketable title. Although the investor's allegations appear to be true, he can only seek a remedy that arises from the deed—not the contract that merged with the deed. As a result, the original seller is likely to prevail.*

*The investor likely would have prevailed had he instead sued the original seller for breaching a covenant of title契約中保證產權無瑕疵的承諾條款 contained within the warranty deed that he received.

(Choice B) A seller may be liable for reasonably foreseeable damages that arise from a breach of a warranty in the deed or from fraudulent assertions in the land-sale contract. But neither ground has been asserted by the investor in this case.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the doctrine of merger, all obligations contained within the land-sale contract merge into the deed and can be enforced thereafter only if they are incorporated into the deed.
questions.zh-question:
一位卖方签订书面合同，将一块土地出售给一位投资人。合同没有提及所转让所有权的品质。随后，卖方和投资人完成了交易，卖方将一份担保契据交付给了投资人。

此后不久，该土地的价值急剧上涨。投资人与一位买方签订书面合同，欲将该土地出售。投资人与买方之间的合同明确规定，投资人将转让一份可销售的所有权。买方的律师发现，该土地的所有权不具有可销售性，并且在原始卖方转让给投资人时就不具有可销售性。买方因此拒绝完成交易。

投资人以原始卖方未能转让可销售的所有权，导致其无法将土地出售给后来的买方而遭受损失为由，对原始卖方提起违约之诉，要求损害赔偿。

在此诉因上，哪一方可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 投资人，因为法律默示此类合同中包含一项所有权具有可销售性的契约。
zh-choices.B: 投资人，因为原始卖方对所有可合理预见的损害承担责任。
zh-choices.C: 原始卖方，因为她关于所有权的合同义务已并入契据。
zh-choices.D: 原始卖方，因为她没有明确同意转让可销售的所有权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property / Contracts
核心考点：合并原则 (Doctrine of Merger)

在不动产法中，土地买卖合同（Contract）中的条款在交割（Closing）并交付契据（Deed）后，即被视为“并入”契据之中。

这意味着：一旦买方接受了契据，合同中的默示条款（如可销售所有权）即告终止。买方此后只能依据契据中的条款（Covenants in the Deed）进行起诉，而不能再依据合同起诉。

案情逻辑推演
1
合同阶段：
原始卖方与投资人签订合同。虽然未提及所有权质量，但法律默示包含Marketable Title（可销售所有权/适销所有权）的保证。
2
交割阶段 (关键点)：
卖方交付了Warranty Deed（担保契据），投资人接受了。此时，合同义务并入契据。合同中关于“可销售所有权”的默示保证随之消灭。
3
诉讼阶段：
投资人起诉的理由是“违约” (Breach of Contract)，指控卖方未能根据合同转让可销售所有权。
4
结论：
由于合同已并入契据，投资人不能再基于合同起诉。他本应依据担保契据中的条款（如 Covenant of Seisin 或 Covenant Against Encumbrances）起诉。因为起诉依据错误，卖方胜诉。
选项深度解析
✅ 选项 C (正确答案)

“原始卖方胜诉，因为她关于所有权的合同义务已并入契据。”

这是对 Doctrine of Merger 的直接应用。合同中的默示保证在交割后不再独立存在。如果契据本身没有包含同样的保证（尽管本案是Warranty Deed，通常包含，但原告起诉的是合同违约而非契据违约），或者原告起诉的依据仅限于合同，则原告败诉。

❌ 选项 A (常见陷阱)

虽然法律确实在土地买卖合同中默示了“可销售所有权”的契约，但这项权利仅在交割前（Pre-closing）有效。一旦交割完成，该权利即被合并原则切断。

❌ 选项 B (无关干扰项)

“可预见的损害”是计算赔偿额的标准，前提是必须先确立责任（Liability）。由于合并原则免除了卖方在合同项下的责任，损害赔偿的计算就无从谈起。

❌ 选项 D (法律错误)

该选项声称卖方没有明确同意转让可销售所有权。这是错误的，因为除非另有约定，所有土地买卖合同都默示包含可销售所有权的保证。卖方胜诉不是因为没有保证，而是因为该保证在合同阶段结束后已失效。

💡 MBE 考试技巧：
遇到不动产买卖纠纷，首先画出时间轴：
1. 合同签订后，交割前：买方依据合同条款（Marketable Title）主张权利。
2. 交割后（拿到Deed）：买方必须依据契据条款（Deed Covenants）主张权利。

本题中，题目明确指出已经 "delivered a warranty deed"（已交割），且原告起诉的是 "breach of contract"（违约）。这种阶段与诉因的不匹配是解题的关键。
